source.title: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3

claim: AlphaFold 3 predicts joint structures for complexes that can include proteins, nucleic acids, small molecules, ions, and modified residues.
evidence: The article describes one diffusion-based model for joint structure prediction across proteins, nucleic acids, ligands, ions, and modified residues.
label: supports

source.title: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3

claim: AlphaFold 3 is limited to predicting interactions between proteins and cannot model nucleic acids or small molecules.
evidence: The article describes one diffusion-based model for joint structure prediction across proteins, nucleic acids, ligands, ions, and modified residues.
label: contradicts
notes: The evidence explicitly lists non-protein molecular types.

source.title: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3

claim: AlphaFold 3 outperformed every specialized comparison method in every evaluated category.
evidence: The main text reports substantially higher performance than strong specialized methods in all but one evaluated category.
label: partially_supports
notes: Broad superiority is supported, but the universal quantifier is not.

source.title: Accurate proteome-wide missense variant effect prediction with AlphaMissense

claim: AlphaMissense classified 89% of possible human missense variants as likely benign or likely pathogenic.
evidence: The study provides proteome-wide predictions and assigns likely benign or likely pathogenic labels to 89% of missense variants.
label: supports

source.title: Accurate proteome-wide missense variant effect prediction with AlphaMissense

claim: AlphaMissense was explicitly trained on the genetic and experimental benchmark labels used to report its performance.
evidence: The model was fine-tuned using human and primate population-frequency data and was evaluated on genetic and experimental benchmarks without explicit training on those benchmark data.
label: contradicts

source.title: Accurate proteome-wide missense variant effect prediction with AlphaMissense

claim: The study established regulatory approval for AlphaMissense as a standalone clinical diagnostic test.
evidence: The article reports a research model and a community database of pathogenicity predictions; the summarized results do not address regulatory approval.
label: not_addressed
notes: A research result does not establish regulatory status.

source.title: A draft human pangenome reference

claim: The first draft human pangenome contained 47 phased diploid assemblies from genetically diverse individuals.
evidence: The consortium's draft comprises 47 phased diploid genome assemblies selected from a genetically diverse cohort.
label: supports

source.title: A draft human pangenome reference

claim: Using the draft pangenome increased small-variant discovery errors by 34% compared with GRCh38 workflows.
evidence: When used for short-read analysis, the draft pangenome reduced small-variant discovery errors by 34% relative to GRCh38-based workflows.
label: contradicts

source.title: A draft human pangenome reference

claim: The 47-genome draft completely represented all global human genetic diversity.
evidence: The 47 assemblies were selected for diversity but form a subset of a larger planned panel intended to better capture global diversity.
label: partially_supports
notes: Diversity is supported; completeness is not.

source.title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Obesity without Diabetes

claim: In SELECT, weekly semaglutide reduced the primary composite cardiovascular endpoint compared with placebo in people with overweight or obesity and no diabetes.
evidence: Among participants with established cardiovascular disease, overweight or obesity, and no diabetes, events occurred in 6.5% with semaglutide and 8.0% with placebo; the hazard ratio was 0.80.
label: supports
notes: Population and endpoint must remain attached.

source.title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Obesity without Diabetes

claim: SELECT demonstrated the cardiovascular benefit specifically in participants with type 2 diabetes.
evidence: The trial enrolled 17,604 adults with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity but explicitly excluded a history of diabetes.
label: contradicts

source.title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Obesity without Diabetes

claim: Semaglutide prevents major cardiovascular events in every adult with obesity.
evidence: The benefit was observed in adults aged at least 45 years who already had cardiovascular disease, had overweight or obesity, and had no diabetes.
label: partially_supports
notes: Effect claim is broader than the trial population and absolute wording is unsupported.

source.title: Donanemab in Early Symptomatic Alzheimer Disease: The TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 Randomized Clinical Trial

claim: Donanemab significantly slowed clinical progression over 76 weeks in participants with early symptomatic Alzheimer disease and amyloid and tau pathology.
evidence: The randomized trial found significantly slower clinical progression at 76 weeks in low-to-medium tau and combined tau populations receiving donanemab.

source.title: Donanemab in Early Symptomatic Alzheimer Disease: The TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 Randomized Clinical Trial

claim: No amyloid-related imaging abnormalities occurred among participants receiving donanemab.
evidence: Amyloid-related edema or effusion occurred in 24.0% of the donanemab group and 2.1% of the placebo group, with symptomatic cases in the treatment group.

source.title: Donanemab in Early Symptomatic Alzheimer Disease: The TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 Randomized Clinical Trial

claim: Donanemab cured Alzheimer disease within 76 weeks.
evidence: The trial measured slower worsening on clinical scales; both groups declined, although decline was smaller with donanemab.

source.title: Exagamglogene Autotemcel for Severe Sickle Cell Disease

claim: Twenty-nine of 30 evaluable exa-cel recipients were free from severe vaso-occlusive crises for at least 12 consecutive months.
evidence: Among 30 participants with sufficient follow-up, 29 were free of severe vaso-occlusive crises for at least 12 consecutive months.
label: supports

source.title: Exagamglogene Autotemcel for Severe Sickle Cell Disease

claim: The exa-cel study was a double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial.
evidence: The phase 3 investigation was a single-group, open-label study in patients aged 12 to 35 years.
label: contradicts

source.title: Exagamglogene Autotemcel for Severe Sickle Cell Disease

claim: Exa-cel eliminated severe vaso-occlusive crises in every treated patient for at least 12 months.

source.title: Tirzepatide for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Obesity

claim: In adults with obesity and moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea, tirzepatide produced a substantially larger reduction in apnea-hypopnea index than placebo.
evidence: Across the SURMOUNT-OSA trials, the apnea-hypopnea index fell by as much as 29.3 events per hour with tirzepatide versus 5.3 with placebo.
label: supports

source.title: Tirzepatide for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Obesity

claim: Tirzepatide improved sleep-apnea outcomes without reducing body weight.
evidence: Participants receiving tirzepatide had significant reductions in body weight as well as apnea-hypopnea index and several cardiometabolic measures.
label: contradicts

source.title: Tirzepatide for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Obesity

claim: Tirzepatide cured obstructive sleep apnea in all participants with obesity.
evidence: The trials showed clinically important average improvement, while only a subset reached combined thresholds associated with little or no need for positive-airway-pressure therapy.
label: partially_supports
notes: Average improvement does not imply universal cure.

source.title: Artificial intelligence guided screening for cardiomyopathies in an obstetric population: a pragmatic randomized clinical trial

claim: AI-guided digital-stethoscope screening increased detection of left ventricular systolic dysfunction compared with usual care in the Nigerian obstetric trial.
evidence: Confirmed dysfunction was identified in 4.1% of the intervention arm versus 2.0% with usual care; the reported odds ratio was 2.12 with P equal to 0.032.
label: supports

source.title: Artificial intelligence guided screening for cardiomyopathies in an obstetric population: a pragmatic randomized clinical trial

claim: The 12-lead AI electrocardiogram arm produced a statistically significant increase in detection at the conventional 0.05 level.
evidence: The 12-lead AI electrocardiogram comparison had an odds ratio of 1.75, a confidence interval crossing one, and P equal to 0.125.
label: contradicts
notes: Arithmetic is handled in code; semantics preserve which modality was significant.

source.title: Artificial intelligence guided screening for cardiomyopathies in an obstetric population: a pragmatic randomized clinical trial

claim: AI-guided cardiomyopathy screening is proven effective for every adult population and health system.
evidence: The pragmatic trial enrolled pregnant and postpartum women at six hospitals in Nigeria and evaluated diagnosis during the perinatal period.
label: partially_supports
notes: Effect in one defined setting cannot establish universal performance.

source.title: Evaluation and mitigation of the limitations of large language models in clinical decision-making

claim: In the simulated clinical framework, evaluated state-of-the-art large language models performed worse than physicians and were not ready for autonomous clinical decision-making.
evidence: Across 2,400 curated patient cases and four abdominal pathologies, the evaluated models underperformed physicians and showed workflow and guideline-following limitations.
label: supports

source.title: Evaluation and mitigation of the limitations of large language models in clinical decision-making

claim: The study concluded that current large language models were ready to replace physicians in autonomous clinical decision-making.
evidence: The authors concluded that the evaluated models were not ready for autonomous clinical decision-making and posed serious risks without mitigation.
label: contradicts

source.title: Evaluation and mitigation of the limitations of large language models in clinical decision-making

claim: The study proved that every large language model fails on every possible medical diagnosis.
evidence: The study tested selected state-of-the-art models on four common abdominal pathologies in a simulated environment and found substantial limitations.
label: partially_supports
notes: Negative finding is real but bounded.

source.title: Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease

evidence: The phase 3 trial reported greater amyloid reduction and moderately less decline on cognitive and functional measures with lecanemab at 18 months.

notes: Retains stage, duration, and modest effect language.

source.title: Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease

claim: Lecanemab produced no adverse events related to amyloid imaging abnormalities or infusion reactions.
evidence: The trial reported clinical benefit alongside adverse events, including infusion reactions and amyloid-related imaging abnormalities.

source.title: Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease

claim: Lecanemab reverses cognitive decline in patients at every stage of Alzheimer disease.
evidence: Participants had early disease with confirmed amyloid, and the reported effect was moderately less decline rather than reversal over 18 months.
